label: copy-phase input u (fed-back copy of u)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the input token is u during the copy phase, i.e. when the model just emitted u and it is fed back (99.9% of activation mass on in_tok u, all in phase 2). Never fires in the original phase (even on u inputs) or at the delimiter. Magnitude and firing rate grow with absolute step t / sequence length: steps after an early u in short sequences (L=3-5, t<8) are often silent, which accounts for most false positives (~18%); the strongest activations are at late copy positions in L=8-9 sequences. Rare weak misses on fed-back g, 2, i.

issues: The claims hold up. On dev the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases, puts 99.9% of its activation mass on in_tok u, and its firing rate rises with t and L. On test the predicate scores P 0.817, R 0.996, F1 0.898, matching the reported numbers.

The false positives follow a smooth position effect, not a separate category. Copy-phase u at t<7 with L<=5 has precision 0.40. Copy-phase u at t<7 with L>=6 has none (precision 0). Precision rises steadily with t. This matches the explanation's caveat about early u in short sequences.

No hidden condition based on history was found. Precision barely changes with in_count (0.80 when 1, 0.86 when 2 or more), with a digit as the previous token (0.84), or with u as the previous token (0.91).
The misses are scattered and weak (280 test steps, 0.1% of mass) on fed-back g, 2, p and 0. Copy-phase g alone gives F1 0.002. This is noise.
Optional small refinement: adding t>=6 raises test F1 from 0.898 to 0.908 by dropping the low-t tail. The gain is minor and does not change the label.
